summary: Overall: well‑executed, fully archived preregistered run with excellent artifact provenance. The experiment faithfully implements the preregistered shared_initial_candidate design and documents results and failures. However the executed generation semantics (single shared LLM candidate reused across conditions) and an observed ceiling baseline success rate (1.00) substantially change the inferential target from typical “agentic vs baseline” comparisons. The manuscript must more clearly and prominently limit its claims and wording to the executed estimand (effect of downstream tool/validator processing given identical LLM candidates). Required manuscript edits (title/abstract/contribution statements and hypothesis interpretation) are needed before finalisation.
critical_issues: Title and abstract risk misrepresenting the executed estimand: the paper markets a Tool‑Augmented Agent vs LLM‑Only comparison while the run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single LLM generation reused for both conditions). This makes the experimental contrast ‘‘downstream tool/verifier processing on identical candidates’’ rather than independent agentic generation; the current title/abstract are liable to mislead reviewers/readers.

The preregistered primary inferential goal (detecting a +0.20 absolute paired success difference) relied on an assumed baseline success ≈0.60. Observed baseline success was 1.00 (299/299), producing a ceiling effect that invalidates the original power assumptions and renders the preregistered primary hypothesis uninformative as originally framed—this must be explicitly stated as an untestable/failed confirmatory contrast in the manuscript, not merely discussed as a caveat.

Although the manuscript does disclose the shared_initial_candidate design, the placement and wording downplay its centrality. The executed findings (n11=299, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0) must be presented only as answering the narrower question implied by shared generation semantics. Any language suggesting broader production‑level or agentic‑generation benefits should be removed or reframed as future work.
required_revisions: Revise the paper title, abstract opening sentences, and the final paragraph(s) of the Introduction/Contributions so they explicitly and unambiguously state that generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate and that the experiment therefore measures downstream verifier/tool processing of identical LLM candidates (not independent agentic generation). Example resolvable edit: add ‘‘(shared_initial_candidate: single LLM generation reused across conditions)’’ in title subtitle or first sentence of abstract and repeat where contributions are listed.

Mark the preregistered primary hypothesis as effectively untestable under the observed data: add a concise, explicit statement in Methods/Results that the observed baseline success rate = 1.00 violates the power assumption, producing a ceiling effect and preventing detection of the preregistered minimally important effect; report that H1 as answered for the executed estimand (no downstream difference) but that the originally hypothesized agentic‑generation contrast remains untested and should be treated as future work. Cite deterministic_reconciliation.json and the contingency table as archival evidence.

Tighten all contribution and conclusion claims to the executed estimand. Remove or reword any phrase in the title, abstract, conclusions, or contribution bullets implying that the run compared independent agentic tool‑augmented generation to LLM‑only generation. Ensure the Disclosure Statement repeats the shared_initial_candidate semantics prominently (it is present but must be emphasized so readers cannot misinterpret the test).
optional_revisions: Add a short, artifact‑anchored sentence in Results or Discussion hypothesizing why the declared model produced near‑perfect valid outputs for the chosen task bank (e.g., model strength vs task difficulty), and refer to the task‑difficulty fields in representative task manifests to support this; label this speculative and exploratory.

Add an explicit pointer (file path + hash) in the manuscript body (Methods or Reproducibility paragraph) to the deterministic_reconciliation.json, the paired_contingency_table.csv, and the two failed episode log entries (pair‑000269) so reviewers can quickly locate the authoritative artifacts.

In Discussion, include a concrete preregistered follow‑up recipe (machine‑readable) that would test agentic per‑condition generation (switch to independent per‑condition generation semantics, increase sample size or task difficulty, and predefine multi‑model replication), and reference it as the natural next confirmatory preregistration.
